[Model and example](../vignettes/05a_residual_risk/05a_residual_risk.ipynb) · [All benchmarks](../benchmark.qmd)

The residual-risk model estimates, for a successful one-second ball drive, the probability that the individual possession ends in a loss. The [model vignette](../vignettes/05a_residual_risk/05a_residual_risk.ipynb) introduces the conditional terminal-outcome task, its likelihood, the relationship to the action-selection features, feature importance and an executable example. This benchmark documents the outcome conventions, the cohort, the training protocol, the predictive evaluation and the final fit. The classifier is a native XGBoost model with a binary logistic objective ([Chen and Guestrin, 2016](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.02754)).

## Evaluation cohort

Successful canonical one-second carries are identified as described in [Possessions and checkpoints](../vignettes/06_possession_and_checkpoint_setup/06_possession_and_checkpoint_setup.ipynb). Each eligible state is a completed one-second ball drive within an outfield player's individual possession, and shorter interrupted tails are not included. The target is the **terminal outcome of that individual possession**.

Terminal outcomes are verified with the same conventions as **Pass Selection** and **Ball Drive**: terminal passes require verified continuous direct reception, and direct possession losses follow the OBE verification of the physical carry model. No additional pass-duration, curvature or unknown-context filter is applied. A failed terminal pass or a direct `possession_loss` is labeled **loss ($Y=1$)**, and a completed terminal pass is labeled **no loss ($Y=0$)**. Individual possessions ending in a **clearance** ($Y=1$) or a **foul suffered** ($Y=0$) are also included, while those ending in a shot are excluded. Clearances are treated as terminal losses under the assumption that they are induced by defensive pressure.

The cohort contains **7,820 successful one-second ball drive states**, of which **1,423 end in a terminal individual loss (18.20%)**, across ten matches and **3,975 individual possessions**. A possession can contribute more than one state.

| Terminal individual outcome | States | Individual possessions | Loss label |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Completed pass | 6,258 | 3,214 | 0 |
| Failed pass | 742 | 397 | 1 |
| Direct possession loss | 654 | 286 | 1 |
| Clearance | 27 | 14 | 1 |
| Foul suffered | 139 | 64 | 0 |

## Features

The model uses **31 features**: the action-selection feature family with two changes. The number of completed carries is replaced by the elapsed time since individual control began, and the action-selection probability of carrying is added. The shared feature definitions are in the [action-selection vignette](../vignettes/04_action_selection/04_action_selection.ipynb).

The upstream components (physics, pass, destination-choice, xT and BCOS models) are fitted separately for each evaluation fold. The action-selection probability of carrying is cross-fitted so that no state is scored by a model that was trained on it. Training states are scored by three action-selection refits, each fitted on four of the six training matches and omitting the other two, and validation and test states are scored by the action-selection model of the same outer fold. This cross-fitting applies to the action-selection probabilities and not to the whole upstream stack.

## Model selection and validation

The evaluation uses five match-disjoint outer folds with **6 fitting + 2 validation + 2 test** matches. The validation matches support upstream calibration and the selection of the downstream model, and the test matches are used only for evaluation.

The XGBoost grid covers maximum depth (3, 4, 6, 8), minimum child weight (1, 5, 20), L2 regularization (0.1, 1, 3, 10) and learning rate (0.03, 0.05, 0.10), giving **144 configurations × 5 folds = 720 fits**. Row and column subsampling are 0.8, training allows at most 2,000 trees, and early-stopping patience is 100. Validation cross entropy selects the configuration and the tree prefix before testing. There is no resampling, class weighting or custom derivative. A single positive temperature can be fitted on the validation matches with the trees held fixed ([Guo et al., 2017](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.04599)), and test scores are not used to select it.

## Predictive performance

| Variant | CE | Null CE | Gain over null | Brier | AUC | Quantile ECE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **Native** | **0.419506** | **0.475594** | **11.793%** | **0.131390** | **0.73950** | **1.053%** |
| Temperature-scaled | 0.419773 | 0.475594 | 11.737% | 0.131395 | 0.73963 | 1.315% |

The native model is retained, since temperature scaling does not improve cross entropy or ECE here. In each fold the null model predicts the terminal-loss frequency of the fitting matches. Metrics pool the held-out states, and ECE uses ten equal-count pooled bins weighted by their counts.

![Five-fold pooled conditional residual-risk calibration.](../figures/residual_risk_pooled_calibration.png){#fig-residual-risk-calibration}

Remaining possession time is retrospective and is not a predictor. A diagnostic on the verified cohort reports four remaining-time groups and an equal-possession weighting sensitivity.

## Feature importance

Feature importance is the **total XGBoost split gain**, normalized within each ensemble, with one-hot levels grouped under their original feature. The figure shows the production model and the five outer-fold models, and fold ranges describe variation in the fitted rankings.

![Feature importance of the residual-risk model.](../figures/feature_importance_residual_risk.png){#fig-residual-risk-importance}

| Feature | Production gain share | Rank across outer folds |
|---|---:|---:|
| BCOS | 14.21% | 1–4 |
| Opponents ahead, success-weighted | 10.30% | 1–2 |
| One-second ball drive success | 8.83% | 2–4 |
| Expected pass success | 8.01% | 4–25 |
| Team line on pass failure | 5.60% | 10–19 |
| Team xT on pass success | 5.24% | 5–12 |

Accessible space and the spatial configuration of the passing options lead the ranking. BCOS accounts for 14.21% of the total split gain and ranks between first and fourth across folds, and the opponents ahead of likely completed passes contribute 10.30% and rank first or second. The rank of expected pass success varies widely across folds (4–25), so its production share is not a stable ordering. Importance measures describe predictive use and are neither causal effects nor fractions of predictive accuracy.

## Related published work

A targeted literature search on 29 October 2026 found no published cross entropy, null-gain or ECE result for this conditional terminal individual-possession target.

| Work | Published target and result | Difference from this task |
|---|---|---|
| [Gu et al., *Player Pressure Map*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.16235) | Team outcome at 4 s; accuracy 55.8% (tracking), 75.2% (2D PPM), 78.7% (3D PPM) | Team-level horizon, sequence inputs and accuracy as the metric |
| [Dick and Brefeld, *Action rate models for predicting actions in soccer*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10182-022-00435-x) | Next-action rate and turnover before a pass; 75% top-1 turnover hit rate at 1 s before the observed loss | Different labels and metric |
| [Le Coz et al., *A semi-Markov framework for modeling football possessions and temporal expected threat*](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-52938-1) | Team goal probability within a time budget, from event sequences | Different outcome, state and horizon |

## Final fitted model

The production model is a native **118-tree** refit on all 7,820 eligible states. Depth 4, minimum child weight 5, L2 1 and learning rate 0.03 minimize the mean validation cross entropy across the five grids. The best tree prefixes of this configuration in the five folds are 118, 133, 251, 87 and 92, and their median, 118, fixes the refit length without using test scores.

Training values of the action-selection probability of carrying come from five action-selection fits, each fitted on eight of the ten matches and omitting two, and inference uses the installed action-selection model fitted on all ten matches. The production fit is not an out-of-fold evaluation.

For reproducibility, the [metrics](../data/benchmarks/residual_risk/pooled_metrics.csv), [selected configurations](../data/benchmarks/residual_risk/selected_configurations.csv), [fold scores](../data/benchmarks/residual_risk/metrics_by_fold.csv), [per-match scores](../data/benchmarks/residual_risk/metrics_by_match.csv), [remaining-time diagnostic](../data/benchmarks/residual_risk/remaining_time_sensitivity.csv), [literature locators](../data/benchmarks/residual_risk/related_literature.csv), [feature-importance analysis](../data/benchmarks/feature_importance/README.md) and [refit provenance](../docs/residual-risk-refit-provenance.json) are provided as supplementary resources.

## Limitations

Body orientation and posture are not observed in this 2D tracking dataset, and velocity direction is not a measured body orientation (see Gu et al. above). The features summarize current carrier motion, tactical configuration and passing opportunities, and they do not include full recent trajectories or explicit pairwise histories, which recurrent and graph-based action-rate models use (Dick and Brefeld, above).
